{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the IBM hosting agreement — 18 rules assessed

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Base Terms against 18 playbook rules. Eight clauses are acceptable as drafted (indemnification, exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitments, non-solicitation, and the absence of Customer-side restraints generally); seven are deviations we propose to redline; two are missing clauses that must be inserted; and two require further review before we send comments.

The commercially significant points are:

- **Licence scope (§ 12.1)** — the Base Components licence is *revocable* at IBM's discretion and names neither our Affiliates nor contractors acting on our behalf. This is walk-away territory and our top priority.
- **No insurance obligation anywhere in the Agreement** — IBM hosts our environment and processes personal information on our behalf (§ 14.18) with no coverage undertaking. Also walk-away territory; we insert the preferred coverage package.
- **No transition assistance or data return/deletion mechanic** — § 3.5 covers only accrued payments. Unacceptable for a hosted service; we insert a new § 3.6.
- **Audit/investigation right (§ 11.3)** — IBM may investigate suspected AUP violations without frequency limit, without prior notice and with no cost allocation. Walk-away territory; we redline to the fallback (annual, 15 days' notice, IBM bears costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%).
- **Assignment asymmetry (§ 14.10)** — we need consent for almost any transfer; IBM is unrestricted and could assign to a competitor.
- **Liability caps (§§ 9.1–9.2)** are mutual and 12-month-fees based with indemnities outside the cap (favourable), but confidentiality breaches are capped and there is no gross negligence / wilful misconduct carve-out.
- **Governing law (§ 14.3)** selects New York law (our preference) but the Agreement designates no forum at all; we add exclusive New York County venue.

On the favourable side, IBM's IP indemnity (§ 8.1) is effectively uncapped, we hold a one-month convenience exit (§ 3.4), and no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or non-solicit obligation binds us.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary of position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (at fallback) | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | Express IP defence and indemnity with permitted customer-side exclusions; all fallback remedies present; § 9.1(a) places indemnity payments outside the monetary cap, so effectively uncapped. Noted only: no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross-negligence indemnity, and our § 8.2 indemnity is broader than preferred. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14.10 Assignment | Consent obligation binds Customer only (with a narrow merger carve-out); IBM may assign freely, including to a competitor. Fails the fallback, which requires mutual consent for non-successor assignments. Redline: extend the carve-out to affiliates and asset sales, add IBM-side consent, a competitor bar, and confirmation that a change of control gives IBM no termination right. *(Verification: repaired.)* |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (§ 7.0 Materials; § 14.18) | Ownership split is acceptable (we own Type I; IBM owns Type II), so the walk-away is not triggered. But the Type II licence is not perpetual, is confined to our Enterprise, and omits modification and sublicensing rights; § 14.18 lets IBM and its Enterprise use our contact information for marketing and research. Redline: perpetual, royalty-free, modifiable/sublicensable Type II licence and IBM data rights limited to providing the Services. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 12.1 License | Base Components licence is *revocable*, runs to Bluefly only, and § 14.17 bars implied licences, so Affiliates and contractors are excluded with no cure. Redline: extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, delete "revocable", add perpetuity for paid-up licences and breach-only termination for subscriptions. Successor transfer is already covered by § 14.10. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No exclusivity, sole-source or requirements obligation; § 14.16 confirms each party may contract with others. § 14.11 (no resale) and § 12.1 scope limits are use restrictions, not exclusive dealing. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint. § 14.11, § 12.1 and § 14.19 are licence-scope and delivery-location terms only. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | Unlimited, unannounced investigation right with no cost allocation, reinforced by our open-ended obligation to supply all relevant information on request. Redline to the fallback: once per year, 15 days' prior notice, IBM bears costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%. Preferred independent-auditor/off-site terms held in reserve. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York substantive law matches our preference, but no forum is designated anywhere (only generic "court of competent jurisdiction" references). Redline: add exclusive state and federal courts in New York County with the customary injunctive-relief carve-out; law sentence untouched. Jury waiver (§ 14.4) and two-year limitation (§ 14.14) noted only. |
| Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing (walk-away)** | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance clause exists; § 14.12, § 5.3 and § 14.18 allocate risk and describe security without any coverage undertaking. Insert new § 14.21: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request. |
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Caps are mutual at the greater of USD 100,000 or 12 months' charges, indemnities sit outside the cap and consequential damages are mutually excluded — but confidentiality breaches are capped (§ 6 makes §§ 9–10 prevail over the NDA) and there is no gross negligence / wilful misconduct carve-out. Redline: one mutual carve-out sentence at the fallback. USD 100,000 floor and absence of data-protection/IP carve-outs noted, not pressed. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Only a reasonable care and skill undertaking, with no warranty period, no conformance-to-documentation warranty and no remedy; §§ 5.2 and 5.4 make it exclusive and add "AS IS" disclaimers. Redline inside § 5.1 (to sit within the § 5.2 carve-in): 90-day software conformance warranty, 30-day Services warranty, repair/replace-or-refund remedy. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | § 3.5 covers accrued payments only; no exit assistance, export, return or deletion obligation anywhere. Insert new § 3.6: six months' assistance at then-current rates, return of Content in machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter (using the defined term "Content"). |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Needs review** | § 3.2 Renewal | Automatic renewal with a 90-day non-renewal notice window exceeds our 60-day fallback ceiling. Single numeral edit proposed to reach the fallback. No renewal price-increase mechanic exists, so the uplift element is satisfied. Escalation point: any Service Option Attachment with a term over 12 months produces an automatic multi-year renewal. *(Verification: fail — must be re-run before issue.)* |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Our one-month convenience exit is better than the fallback and IBM has no mid-term convenience right. The failure is the open-ended early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A; proposed cap of three months' charges for the terminated Services. Pro-rata refund of prepaid charges noted, not redlined. *(Verification: fail — must be re-run before issue.)* |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No best-price, most-favoured-customer, disclosure or right-to-match undertaking. IBM's only pricing right is a forward-looking change after 12 months on 90 days' notice with a Customer termination right. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant (preferred) | § 4.1 Charges | Charges arise only for Services actually ordered; no minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic; § 11.5 allocates capacity planning only. We hold exits under §§ 3.2 and 3.4. Diligence point: Attachment A (not in the reviewed text) may contain early termination charges. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.8 Personnel | No solicitation, no-hire or recruitment restriction; § 14.8 addresses supervision and subcontracting only. Resist introduction; if added, hold to the mutual 12-month fallback with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | § 3.4(b) conditions our convenience exit on uncapped early termination charges set in documents outside the Base Terms, and nothing makes this the sole liquidated amount. Redline to the fallback (three months' charges, sole liquidated amount) rather than deletion, because § 3.3 cross-refers to § 3.4(b). Late payment fees (§ 4.2) and the § 9.2 cap are not liquidated damages. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points our playbook treats as walk-away territory. They should be resolved before signature and, if IBM refuses, escalated rather than conceded.

1. **§ 12.1 — revocable licence excluding Affiliates and contractors.** A licence revocable at IBM's discretion, with no affiliate or contractor coverage and no implied licences (§ 14.17), is walk-away territory and also fails the fallback.
2. **No insurance obligation (absence; nearest provision § 14.12).** IBM hosts our environment and processes personal information on our behalf with no coverage undertaking — walk-away territory under the rule.
3. **§ 11.3 — unlimited, unannounced investigation right.** Verification without frequency limits, prior notice or cost allocation is walk-away territory; the fallback (annual / 15 days / cost shifting) is our landing zone.
4. **§ 3.2 — multi-year automatic renewal exposure (escalation).** Any Service Option Attachment with a term exceeding 12 months would auto-renew for that multi-year period. Fix with a 12-month renewal cap or escalate.

For completeness: the IP walk-away (assignment of Customer IP) is **not** triggered — we take ownership of Type I Materials under § 7.0.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-run verification on the two `needs_review` items (RENEWAL § 3.2 and T4C § 3.4)** before any markup leaves our side; both currently carry a failed verification and should not be issued as drafted.
2. **Obtain Attachment A and all Service Option Attachments / Order Forms.** They drive the early termination charges under §§ 3.3, 3.4(b) (relevant to both T4C and LD), the pricing under § 4.1, and the attachment terms that determine the § 3.2 renewal exposure. We cannot close MINCOMMIT, T4C or LD without them.
3. **Issue the redline in priority order:** § 12.1 licence scope, new insurance section (§ 14.21), new transition/data-return section, § 11.3 audit limits, § 14.10 assignment mutuality, § 9 confidentiality and wilful misconduct carve-out, § 5.1 warranties, § 14.3 venue, Type II licence and § 14.18 data-use limits, § 3.4(b) charge cap.
4. **Confirm the confidentiality interaction.** Section 6 makes §§ 9 and 10 prevail over the separate confidentiality agreement for information in the hosting environment; confirm with the deal team whether any separate NDA terms need conforming.
5. **Hold reserve positions.** For AUDIT we have not yet asked for independent-auditor, off-site or no-system-access terms; for WARRANTY we have targeted the fallback only. Both remain available if IBM resists.
6. **Watch-list for negotiation:** resist any late introduction of exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or non-solicitation language — we currently sit at the preferred position on all five."}
